infl_ens.inflgame.router.core¶

Main InfluencerRouter class.

The router is the consumer-facing object: configure it once with a trait space, a list of agents, and a competitive reach \(\sigma\), then call route() or route_batch() per query.

Classes

InfluencerRouter(trait_space, agents, sigma)

Route queries to agents via the influencer-game allocation rule.
class infl_ens.inflgame.router.core.InfluencerRouter(trait_space, agents, sigma, policy='argmax')[source]¶

Bases: object

Route queries to agents via the influencer-game allocation rule.

Given N agents with strategic positions \(x_1, \dots, x_N\) in a trait space \(\mathbb{B}\), an incoming query is embedded at \(b^* \in \mathbb{B}\) and routed according to a policy:

  • 'argmax': deterministic, picks \(\arg\max_i f_i(x_i, b^*)\). Corresponds to the \(\sigma \to 0\) winner-takes-all limit of the influencer game.

  • 'proportional': stochastic, samples agent \(i\) with probability \(G_i(\mathbf{x}, b^*)\). Matches the game’s payoff semantics exactly and provides natural load balancing.

Agent positions can be set manually, initialised from calibration sets (see RouterAgent.from_calibration()), or optimised by the trainer in infl_ens.training.router_training.

Parameters:

  • trait_space (TraitSpace) – Discretised trait space and resource distribution.

  • agents (Sequence[RouterAgent]) – Router agents. Each position must have shape (trait_space.L,).

  • sigma (float | numpy.ndarray) – Competitive reach. Scalar (isotropic) or shape (L,) (axis-aligned anisotropic). Shared across agents to preserve the kernel-symmetry assumption of Theorems 1–5.

  • policy (str) – 'argmax' or 'proportional'.

Raises:

ValueError – If policy is unrecognised, agents is empty, sigma has the wrong shape, or any agent’s position has the wrong dimensionality.

property positions: ndarray¶

Stacked agent positions.

Returns:

Matrix of shape (N, L).

Return type:

numpy.ndarray

property sigma_scalar: float¶

Geometric-mean competitive reach across axes.

For isotropic cov this is exactly \(\sigma\); for anisotropic diagonal cov it is the geometric mean of the axis reaches, used as a single-number summary in is_stable().

Returns:

Effective scalar \(\sigma\).

Return type:

float

expected_utilities()[source]¶

Expected utility \(u_i(\mathbf{x})\) for each agent.

Returns:

Utility vector, shape (N,). Sums to one in expectation.

Return type:

numpy.ndarray

is_stable()[source]¶

Whether the configured \(\sigma\) clears the symmetric stability threshold.

Tests \(\sigma > \sigma_0^*\) (Corollary 8, multivariate form). This is a necessary condition for the symmetric Nash equilibrium of an \(N\)-agent MV-Gaussian game to be locally asymptotically stable on this resource landscape; it does not certify any specific asymmetric configuration.

Returns:

True if the configured reach exceeds the threshold.

Return type:

bool

route(query, rng=None)[source]¶

Route a single query to one agent.

Ties under the 'argmax' policy are broken uniformly at random rather than by index order. This matters at clone-start: when all positions are identical, \(G_i \equiv 1/N\) and every agent ties; deterministic argmax would always pick agent 0 and break the intended symmetric initial condition.

Parameters:

  • query (str) – Raw query text.

  • rng (numpy.random.Generator | None) – Optional generator for proportional sampling and argmax tiebreaking. Defaults to numpy.random.default_rng(); call-site is responsible for seeding via infl_ens.utils.seeding.seed_all().

Returns:

Selected agent.

Return type:

RouterAgent

route_batch(queries, rng=None, *, routing_weight='G')[source]¶

Route a batch of queries.

Ties under the 'argmax' policy are broken uniformly at random per query; see route() for rationale.

Parameters:

  • queries (Sequence[str]) – Raw query texts.

  • rng (numpy.random.Generator | None) – Optional generator for sampling / tiebreaks.

  • routing_weight (str) –

    Per-trait routing-probability weighting.

    • 'G' (default): standard proportional allocation \(p_i \propto G_i\). This is the canonical Lovett & Fu (2024) allocation rule and what every prior call assumes.

    • 'G_times_1mG': strategic-gradient-matched weighting \(p_i \propto G_i(1 - G_i)\). Routes more queries to contested traits and fewer to traits where one agent already dominates. In expectation over a batch sampled from \(B\), the resulting position drift matches the strategic gradient \(\nabla_{x_i} u_i\) (up to \(\Sigma^{-1}\) and a normaliser). Reduces to 'G' at clone-start (where \(G_i \equiv 1/N\)).

    Only honoured under policy='proportional'; policy='argmax' always uses \(G\) directly.

Returns:

List of selected agents, one per query, in input order.

Return type:

list[RouterAgent]

Raises:

ValueError – If routing_weight is not a recognised mode.
